items.title: Climate Change and Environment Committee (CCEC) Report Template Recommendation, DSD-2026-297
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-297, dated July 15, 2026, recommending that staff be directed as part of the next corporate report template review to consider a climate lens, specifically greenhouse gas emission reductions; and that an item be added to Council reports, where appropriate, to promote and/or foster a culture of applying a climate action lens to all decisions, initiatives and programs. 

A. Ciprani, Corporate Sustainability Officer was in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic entered the meeting at this time.

items.title: Public Hearing Matters under the Planning Act (advertised)
notes: This is a formal public meeting to consider applications under the Planning Act. In accordance with the Ontario Planning Act, only the applicant or owner of land affected by the planning applications, a specified person, or a public body, and or the Minister may appeal most decisions.  If you do not make a verbal submission to the Committee or Council, or make a written submission prior to City Council making a decision on the proposal, you may not be entitled to appeal the decision of the City of Kitchener to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT), and may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT. To understand your right of appeal, if any, or for further clarification regarding appeals, please see the Ontario Land Tribunal website.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Application ZBA25/025/B/EW and Major Modification to Draft Plan of Subdivisions 30T-18201 and 30T-18202, DSD-2026-282
notes:
The Committee considered Zoning By-law Amendment Application ZBA25/025/B/EW and associated Major Modification Applications to Draft Plans of Subdivision 30T-18201 and 30T-18202, as outlined in Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-282.

E. Wittmann, Senior Planner, provided an overview of the report. T. Malone-Wright, Manager, Development Approvals, was in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

D. Riley, Kitchener Green Development, was in attendance in support of the application and staff recommendation.

Councillor S. Davey left the meeting at this time. 

In response to questions from the Committee, D. Riley advised that the proposed lot depths reflect current market preferences for smaller yards that require less maintenance. He noted that the design provides additional green space along the street and allows for improved interior home layouts, while contributing positively to the overall streetscape. 

Councillor S. Davey entered the meeting at this time.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Application ZBA21/019/S/BB, Draft Plan of Vacant Land Condominium 30CDM-24215, 26 Stanley Avenue and 31 Schweitzer Street, DSD-2026-283
notes:
The Committee considered Zoning By-law Amendment Application ZBA/21/019/S/BB and Draft Plan of Vacant Land Condominium Application 30CDM-24215 for Newo Holdings Inc., regarding the lands municipally addressed as 26 Stanley Avenue and 31 Schweitzer Street, as outlined in Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-283. It was noted a written submission was received by J. McCash, A. Romotz, B. Kreller, and M. and M. Schaefer.

E. Wittmann, Senior Planner, provided an overview of the report. T. Malone-Wright, Manager, Development Approvals, was in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

E. Wittmann noted since the agenda was published the Region of Waterloo requested an additional condition, thus staff are proposing an amendment to the staff recommendation, to include an additional condition to include a holding provision requiring a Record of Site Condition and clarified the conditions that must be satisfied prior to residential development proceeding on the site.

K. Barisdale, GSP Group, was in attendance in support of the application and staff recommendation. J. Owens and C. Owens were also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

M. Schaefer and J. Orsan addressed the Committee in opposition to the application, citing concerns regarding traffic impacts, increased density, municipal servicing, future road connections, neighbourhood compatibility and design, tree preservation and removals, and the proximity of the development to the adjacent cemetery. Concerns were expressed that the proposed density and lack of parkland could lead to inappropriate use of the cemetery as open space for recreational activities and may contribute to crime and safety concerns.

In response to questions from the Committee, E. Wittmann advised that Bridge Street is a Regional road and that the Region had not identified any concerns regarding road capacity or future widening through its review of the application. He further noted that City transportation staff were satisfied that the proposed development would not place undue strain on the transportation network based on transportation studies submitted in 2021 and updated in 2023.

E. Wittmann further advised that staff would consult with Parks Planning regarding any future plans for the adjacent park and noted that the City's ongoing Mobility Master Plan may help address broader transportation considerations.

In response to further questions, staff advised that comments from Fire and Emergency Services had been addressed through the application review process. Staff further noted that the development proposes 58 visitor parking spaces, in addition to parking provided for each unit. 

Councillor S. Davey brought forward a motion to refer the recommendation outlined in Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-283, to the August 24, 2026, Council meeting to allow staff additional time to review potential parkland improvements to Schaefer Park, and to continue discussions with the Region regarding traffic concerns.
